findings.reason: the sentence is a scope claim about the code section 9 edits, and a worker satisfying it literally would widen the refusal onto records this host did not launch, changing section 5's landed behaviour beyond the five cases and past the guard `live_worker_pid`'s own docstring gives for refusing to name a foreign pid.
findings.text: section 9 states "The refusal still fires in every arm that reads alive; only its wording changes", but `live_worker_pid` returns `None` before it reads any arm when `_launched_on_this_host(record)` is false (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1290`, helper at `:1151`), and `_env_scan_run_pid` refuses the foreign read as well (`:1329`), so a record whose `launcher_host` is another machine or is unset reads alive yet is refused a launch nowhere; two of the five cases are seeded from the fixture's own `launcher_host: _reading_host()` (`tests/test_a_queued_run_launches_once.py:40`), so none can expose it
